title: What an ack promises: replication and the metadata quorum
dek: An acks=all ack says a record reached the page cache of every in-sync replica and that the in-sync set met a floor. It says nothing about disk. This third part of a five-part teardown reads Apache Kafka 4.4.0 line by line: followers that ack by asking for the next offset, a high watermark that is a minimum, two detectors that decide who leaves the set, a frozen leader that acks what it later deletes, the election ladder down to a last known leader that KIP-966 intends, and the fsyncing metadata log whose loss freezes every one of those lines. All-replica loss here is simulated damage on one host, and its numbers are set by the mock.
byline: 6 November 2026 · Subject: kafka@1156b275 (Apache Kafka 4.4.0) · Part 3 of 5 · Read from the source; measured where this machine allows
description: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 taken apart, part 3: the commit ladder, what an acks=all ack promises, the two ways out of the ISR, leader epochs and truncation, ELR and last-known-leader election, the KRaft metadata log, controller failover, and what quorum loss stops.
og_description: Part 3 of a five-part Kafka teardown at kafka 1156b275 (4.4.0): a fetch offset is an ack, the high watermark is a minimum, one frozen follower stalls every ack, a frozen leader acks what it later deletes, and last-known-leader election runs without consulting the unclean flag, as KIP-966 intends. Tail-loss counts are simulated damage set by the mock, never a loss rate.

badges_callout:
How to read the badges

from the code marks a fact read from the pinned source, cited as repo/path:line: Apache Kafka 4.4.0 (1156b275). Paths are relative to the kafka/ checkout; core/…/ abbreviates core/src/main/scala/kafka/, metadata/…/ abbreviates metadata/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/, and raft/…/ abbreviates raft/src/main/java/org/apache/kafka/raft/. A bare file name is under a tree named nearby. measured here marks output from small clusters on loopback, on a shared 2-vCPU machine with one disk and no iptables. Timings show relative behaviour, never capacity. Each scenario is a single run unless it says otherwise. Tail cuts with truncate -s are simulated damage on one host: they stand in for lost page cache, their loss counts are set by the mock, and no real power cut was run. reconstruction marks a judgement drawn from those sources rather than read in one place. Register ids such as D62 point at the findings register in Part 5.

This is Part 3 of 5 of Kafka, taken apart. Part 1 reads the log on disk; Part 2 follows one request on the wire and through the broker; Part 4 covers producers and consumer groups; Part 5 covers exactly-once, and ends with the findings register.

sections.title: The commit ladder
sections.brief: Followers pull, a fetch offset is an ack, the HW is the lowest LEO across the ISR; min ISR is a floor, not a quorum. replication:F1-F38, X22-X24, TR-replication-1.

sections.title: What the ack promises
sections.brief: Every ISR member's page cache; nothing about any disk, by design. replication:F86-F94, F100, F101, log:F159, TR-replication-8.

sections.title: Two ways out of the ISR
sections.short: Two ways out of the ISR
sections.brief: One frozen follower stalls all acks until one of two detectors fires; past the request timeout the client is told failure for records that exist. replication:F39-F51, F102-F107, X25, TR-replication-2, TR-replication-3.

sections.title: Forks and truncation
sections.brief: Leader epochs make truncation safe for acks=all and fatal for acks=1. replication:F52-F64, F108-F113, TR-replication-4.

sections.title: Elections, ELR, and the last leader
sections.brief: ELR makes empty-ISR elections safe when a clean replica survives; past that, last-known-leader election is intended by KIP-966. All loss counts are mock dials. replication:F65-F85, F114-F125, F129-F132, X26-X28, TR-replication-5/6/7/series.

sections.title: The metadata log
sections.brief: Raft elections on Kafka's pull replication; voters fsync, the controller replays speculatively, every broker reads one log. kraft:F1-F71, F85-F94, F97-F104, X29-X34, TR-kraft-1..4.

sections.title: Losing a controller
sections.brief: The fetch timer dominates failover; a graceful stop is about a quarter of a kill. Relative only. kraft:F105-F111, F127-F130, TR-kraft-5.

sections.title: Losing the quorum
sections.brief: The data plane keeps going, every state change stops. kraft:F72-F84, F95, F96, F112-F126, F131, F132, X35, TR-kraft-6, TR-verify-b-hang.
